source: Gascheau 1843 and Routh 1875 as restated in [R3984] ([R3984], read 2026-10-30); [R3220] ch. 3 (not opened); report reports/lagrange-trojans-2026-10-30.md

mu_crit.basis: (1 - sqrt(23/27)) / 2, the largest m2/(m1+m2) for which L4 and L5 are linearly stable in the circular restricted problem ([R3984], text of section 1)

finite_trojan_rule.basis: the secondary plus the trojan under about 4 percent of the host, as TROY III [R0248] uses it per docs/design/research/oddity-rates.md WR10; the paper's own text for the rule was not read

tadpole_limit_deg.basis: [R3220]: the libration amplitude past which a small-mass tadpole becomes a horseshoe (recalled, not opened)

leading_share_range.basis: no source read: Jupiter's L4 swarm outnumbers its L5 by about 1.6 to 1 (recalled), so the leading share runs from equal to about 0.62; a draw inside it

ecc_max.basis: no source read for a limit: [R0919] keep e under 0.02 in disks and the Jupiter Trojans reach about 0.3 (recalled); a lane measures it with an N-body run

inclination_max_deg.basis: no source read for a limit: Earth Trojans are stable below 15 degrees and between 24 and 37 degrees [R4895]; the Jupiter Trojans reach about 40 (recalled)

hill_separation_k.basis: a pair of planets is Hill stable when their separation exceeds 2 sqrt(3) = 3.46 mutual Hill radii (a result for the planar circular three-body problem, recalled from the stability literature, second-hand); used here as the separation below which another giant or a companion is taken to take the whole swarm

stable_ramp.basis: no source: the share of a swarm that survives a neighbour grows as 1 - exp(-ramp (x - 1)) with x the separation over the Hill-stable one; a ramp of 1 leaves about 70 percent at 2.2 times the limit (two Jupiter-mass giants at a factor of two in distance)

star_limit_margin.basis: no source: a swarm needs its giant inside this fraction of 1/margin of the companion-star stability limit (Holman and Wiegert, `Star.a_crit_au`), because a tadpole librates over a wider range of distance than the planet's own orbit does; a margin of 2 keeps a swarm for a giant inside half the limit

libration_sigma_deg.basis: the Rayleigh scale of the libration amplitude of a swarm's bodies, below the tadpole limit: the Jupiter Trojans' amplitudes are mostly 5 to 25 degrees (recalled, not read); a lane fits it to the catalogue

swarm_ecc_sigma.basis: the Rayleigh scale of the mean eccentricity of a swarm's bodies, cut at ecc_max: the Jupiter Trojans' proper eccentricities are mostly under 0.15 (recalled, not read)

swarm_inclination_sigma_deg.basis: the Rayleigh scale of the mean inclination of a swarm's bodies to the secondary's plane, cut at inclination_max_deg: the Jupiter Trojans reach 40 degrees, most lie under 20 (recalled, not read)
